sentences.text: The appellant-applicant has preferred the application for suspension of sentence under Section 389 Cr.P.C. for suspension [2024:RJ-JD:28775-DB] (2 of 4) [SOSA-614/2023] of sentences during the pendency of the appeal and for release on bail.

3. The basic allegation is that the father of the victim, who was a stonemason, reported that his daughter had gone away with someone on 02.04.2022, and he also apprehended that somebody had enticed her away.
The victim was later recovered, and her statement was recorded as Ex.-3.

In Ex.-3,
which is the first statement of the victim rendered on 09.05.2023, it is reflected that the victim was 12 years old and was living with her father in Himmatnagar.
The victim further stated that she had come into contact with the accused, Kamlesh, and become friends with him.
When her parents were at work, she left for Modasa and then went to Jalod.

From there, she called the accused Kamlesh,
who came to take her.
They then went to Palanpur, where they started living together as husband and wife.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner thereafter has drawn the attention of this Court towards the statement of victim rendered under Section 164 Cr.P.C., which is Exp.-18, and this statement largely corroborates her statement to the police, in which, she acknowledged her friendship with the accused and admitted that she called him and went voluntarily.
The statement also indicates that they subsequently started living together as husband and wife.

Learned counsel for the petitioner thereafter took this Court to the victim's statement during the trial, which is rendered as PW-4, in which, in the examination-in-chief, though she has admitted that she called him on phone and he came and she stayed with him, but in line, she has stated that she was raped, though in cross-examination, she stated that she had voluntarily [2024:RJ-JD:28775-DB] (3 of 4)
[SOSA-614/2023] went and there was no pressure from Kamlesh and she was living with him happily.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner has tried to impress upon this Court by saying that it is a case of complete consent and also submits that the petitioner himself was 21 years old at that time.

6. Learned Public Prosecutor opposed the application for suspension of sentence and submits that despite complete consent, the same would not be relevant because the age of the victim was only 12 years and thus, the act will come into the category of heinous crime.

7. This Court, after carefully examining the record and hearing both parties, is of the opinion that the petitioner himself is of the tender age of 21, and the complete consent of the victim is a mitigating factor for a 12 year old victim, but keeping into consideration the overall factual matrix,
this Court is of the opinion that matter requires consideration.

This Court has also taken note of the fact that the petitioner has been convicted for life imprisonment and the petitioner has been in custody since 11.05.2022, which amounts to a period of about two years.

8. This Court on conjoint consideration of the record, the Ex.-3, the Exp.-18, the trial court statement, two years custody, the age of the petitioner and the other factual matrix of the case,
deems it appropriate to suspend the substantive sentence of the appellant- applicant during the pendency of the appeal.

2 9.

Accordingly, the instant application for suspension of sentence filed under Section 389 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that substantive sentence passed by learned learned Special Judge, POCSO Cases, Dungerpur in Sessions Case [2024:RJ-JD:28775-DB] (4 of 4) [SOSA-614/2023] No.67/2022,
against the appellant-applicant, namely, Kamlesh S/o Magu Bhai,, shall remain suspended till final disposal of the aforesaid appeal and he shall be released on bail, provided he executes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of learned trial Judge for his appearance in this court on 20.08.2024 and whenever ordered to do so till the disposal of the appeal on the conditions indicated below:
1. That he will appear before the trial court in the month of January of every year till the appeal is decided.
2. That if the applicant change the place of residence, he will give in writing his changed address to the trial Court as well as to the counsel in the High Court.
3. Similarly, if the sureties change their address(s) they will give in writing their changed address to the trial court.
10. The learned trial court shall keep the record of attendance of the accused-applicant in a separate file.
Such file be registered as Criminal Misc. Case relating to original case in which the accused- applicant was tried and convicted.
A copy of this order shall also be placed in that file for ready reference.
Criminal Misc. file shall not been taken into account for statistical purpose relating to pendency and disposal of the cases in the trial court.
In case the said accused-applicant does not appear before the trial court, learned trial Judge shall report the matter to the High Court for cancellation of bail.

(MUNNURI LAXMAN),J (DR. PUSHPENDRA SINGH BHATI),J 54-devrajp/-
